answer: Pay for coverage, not headcount. Map each identity's settled work onto a public task graph and pay each vertex a fixed pot split by its occupants. A sybil operator's clones, driven by one strategy, crowd the same profitable vertex — near the cedar-shade arbitrage its model knows — so splitting only divides the same pot thinner. Reaching a second, underserved vertex at the graph's zenith requires a genuinely different capability, counterparty set, and failure risk. Cloning thus cannibalizes itself; only real diversity earns more.
